text:
sam: heads-up — seeing a p99 spike from 17:22 UTC on hosted API. p95 creeping too. started around a small traffic bump but queue depth and latency both climbed fast. kernel selector flips visible in traces.
anya: do we have a recent deploy around that time?
mike: infra-bot shows no deploys at 17:20-17:25. I see increased tail latencies on the g4 pools.
len: posted small profiling snippet — kernel_selector logs show repeated fallbacks to aux kernels for requests >512 tokens, even though most requests are short. suspect sequence-length misclassification + batching ladder.
sam: paste the kernel_selector tail (sanitized):
```
2026-02-10T17:22:10Z kernel_selector: model=redwood-1 size_hint=320 -> choose: main_kernel
2026-02-10T17:22:10Z kernel_selector: model=redwood-1 size_hint=640 -> choose: aux_kernel (fallback)
2026-02-10T17:22:11Z kernel_selector: model=redwood-1 size_hint=320 -> choose: aux_kernel (mismatch)
2026-02-10T17:22:12Z kernel_selector: model=redwood-1 size_hint=64  -> choose: aux_kernel (premature)
```
anya: interesting — aux_kernel latency is ~2x for small sequences in recent perf matrix. why is it getting picked for small seqs?
mike: I see a correlated spike in KV cache miss rate and prefetch churn. Prefetch subsystem is sampling a larger batch window and adding size hints that push theoretical combined sequence to >512. that can shift kernel decision.
len: yep — sampler config rolled ~17:10 that increases coalesce window from 5ms -> 12ms for higher throughput. maybe this allowed diverse seqs to coalesce into mixed-length batches and confused the kernel cost model.
rachel: outputs from the runtime profiler (summary):
- avg queue depth: 21 (baseline 6)
- batch size mean: 14 -> variance high (3..40)
- kvcache hitrate: 78% -> dropped from 94%
- prefetch queue length: doubled
- kernel_switch_count: +300% over baseline
sam: so noisy batching + degraded kvcache priming -> size_hint inflation -> kernel selector flips -> higher per-token op cost -> p99 spike. makes sense.
anya: any tenant/tenant-id correlation? noisy neighbor?
mike: preliminary tenant fingerprinting: 2 tenants account for 60% of the coalesced large-size batches. both are bursty ad-hoc workloads with many long-context requests but also many short ones.
len: I kicked off a targeted trace on one hotspot VM and saw eviction storms in the KV cache: many long requests evict prefix caches used by short requests, causing misses when short requests finally execute.
sre-oncall: mitigation suggestion: temporarily tighten sampler coalesce window for hosted g4 pools to 4ms and enable kernel affinity override to prefer main_kernel for sequences <256. roll this as a hotfix?
sam: +1 for quick sampler rollback. kernel affinity override needs testing but we can gate it to safety-experiments group.
rachel: also recommend increasing kvcache capacity per VM by 10% for the next 30m to reduce eviction churn while we observe.
infra-bot: scaling action initiated: +2 g4 nodes to hosted pool (provisioning...), sampler rollback underway to 5ms coalesce window on targeted hosts.
dev-bot: alert: routing fallback enabled for model redwood-1 -> redwood-1-light for noisy tenants.
anya: after the first 4 minutes of rollback + nodes coming up the p99 dropped from 620ms -> 210ms, p95 back to normal. queue depth fell to ~8. kvcache hitrate recovering.
mike: logs show kernel_switch_count back to baseline and batch variance reduced. looks like sampler change was main trigger.
len: action items: 1) revert sampler config org-wide? or tune with stricter tenant isolation. 2) add a classifier to the kernel selector to consider per-request recent prefetched-kv footprint before size_hint. 3) add an automated kvcache eviction back-pressure metric to trigger temporary capacity bump.
sam: agree. prioritize: (A) revert coalesce change in control plane + add canary for tenant-isolation on coalescing, (B) kernel selector safety rule for small seqs, (C) long-term: smarter prefetch eviction heuristics and tenant-level batching isolation.
anya: I'll own the sampler revert and can add canary flags. len, mike — can you own kernel selector safety rule / perf tests?
mike: happy to take the safety rule and perf microbenchmarks. will instrument with synthetic short/long mix.
len: I'll prototype the kvcache eviction back-pressure metric and draft docs for tenant isolation knobs.
sre-oncall: monitoring: adding alert that fires when batch variance > 20 and kvcache hitrate falls > 10% within 5m.
sam: thanks everyone. will write incident summary and follow-up ticket. tagging this as incident-review. :white_check_mark:
